title: Execution path resilience and observable safeguards
creator: Aisha Menon
description:
Summary: During a mid-February capacity surge we observed a repeated class of inference regressions where requests with similar profiles diverged onto different execution paths and showed ~2-4x tail latency variance. Root cause analysis points to a combination of (1) microbatch threshold hysteresis in the scheduler, (2) probabilistic kernel probing that was gated by a stale affinity score, and (3) an attention autotile heuristic that flips at sequence-length boundaries. Collectively these produced nondeterministic path selection under bursty traffic, which amplified p95/p99 for affected models.

Evidence: Telemetry shows correlated spikes in the 'path_entropy' signal, increased KV cache miss rate for affected flows, and a higher-than-normal rate of 'probe_fallback' events immediately prior to latency spikes. Synthetic repro harness reproduced divergence when we replayed arrival patterns with a 1.2-1.5x burst factor and jittered sequence lengths between 64 and 68 tokens.

Hypothesis (most likely): The scheduler's microbatching window combined with a dithering probe schedule produced transient affinity values. When affinity crossed a brittle autotile threshold the runtime toggled between two kernel families (fused-attn vs quant-attn), causing cache warming penalties and kernel probe fallbacks that increased tail latencies. The decision surface is sensitive to small changes in sequence length and microbatch arrival patterns.

Constraints: We must avoid broad rollbacks to stable kernels (high cost and feature regression). Any mitigation must keep throughput and cost targets intact for Dedicated customers. Changes to probing logic require careful canarying and observability.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Telemetry: Add a compact "path_score" histogram and a per-request "execution_path_trace" token to logs for 7d retention (Owner: L. Ramirez, due 2026-03-18).
- Circuit breaker: Implement a path-entropy circuit-breaker that forces deterministic fallback to the guarded stable kernel when entropy > threshold for > N requests (Owner: K. Zhou, due 2026-03-22).
- Scheduler tuning: Reduce microbatch hysteresis window and add a small smoothing factor to affinity computation (Owner: S. Patel, due 2026-03-20).
- Probing hygiene: Add a deterministic probe sample for 0.1% of requests that records full kernel metrics and KV cache state (Owner: M. Nguyen, due 2026-03-19).
- Canary plan: Deploy the circuit-breaker and telemetry to canary fleet (10% traffic) with 48h observation window, roll forward if no degradation (Owner: E. Carter, due 2026-03-24).
- Synthetic tests: Add a chaos test in the infra-sim harness that replays arrival jitter at 1.2-2x burst with sequence-length micro-perturbation (Owner: A. Menon, due 2026-03-18).
- Documentation & runbook: Update runtime runbook with a step-by-step containment procedure and relevant dashboards/alerts (Owner: L. Ramirez, due 2026-03-21).

Acceptance criteria: New telemetry is ingesting and visible on Console dashboards; circuit-breaker engages under synthetic repro and avoids broad performance regressions on baseline workloads; canary shows reduced p99 variance after rollout; post-deployment comparative benchmarks confirm no >5% throughput regression for Dedicated CI tests.
